_comment: DUO-3222/DUO-3227: the ONE project-level WordPress/PHP/database compatibility statement. WordPress and PHP both use a min-inclusive/max-exclusive range narrowed to the exercised series named in verified, so a version inside the range whose MAJOR.MINOR was never exercised is still refused rather than claimed. The database axis is per-engine instead: engines maps each claimed engine to its own range, because MariaDB 11.x and MySQL 8.4.x are different lines of different products and one bare range could only describe one of them; an engine the map does not name is refused, not compared against another engine's numbers. The agent pre-policy gate and duo doctor block outside these values, and tools/capability-doc.php cross-checks this file against manifests/capabilities/platform.json so the two copies cannot drift -- never independently-maintained numbers.

php.note: Pinned by the sandbox harness's exact Docker tags: each key of verified is a PHP feature-release series, and its value is the exact patch a full live proof ran on (8.3 on wordpress:7.1-php8.3-apache / wordpress:cli-php8.3 -- sandbox/tests/live/regress_core_scope_platform.sh, regress_core_data_boundary.sh, conformance-core). The series map exists here for the same reason it exists on the wordpress axis: this range spans two PHP feature releases (8.3, 8.4), each its own migration with its own deprecations, so a bare range would claim a line nobody ran. PENDING as of this writing: the PHP 8.4 live proof has NOT yet run -- the offline half is green and the 8.4 exercise cell is wired, and that cell asserts the booted PHP_VERSION EQUALS the 8.4 value here exactly, so a wrong proof patch fails loudly on the first live run rather than over-claiming quietly. The 8.4 value 8.4.24 is measured, but from the official php:8.4-cli image (pulled 2026-08-05, the same pull date as the php:8.3-cli image reporting the 8.3.33 this claim already names), NOT yet from wordpress:7.1-php8.4-apache / wordpress:cli-php8.4 -- Docker Hub's unauthenticated rate limit blocked the read-only metadata route to those two at authoring time. If the live matrix fails, the remedy is to drop the 8.4 entry and restore max 8.4.0, never to widen around a failure. A runtime is accepted only when it is inside [8.3.0, 8.5.0) AND its MAJOR.MINOR is one of those exercised series, so an unexercised minor line inside the range is still refused rather than claimed by a bare range. Note that today verified names every series the range contains, so the map narrows nothing operationally right now; it is the shape that makes the next widening a data edit plus one exercise cell instead of a re-argued claim. Patches inside an exercised series are claimed on exactly the basis MariaDB 11.x already is here -- one measured runtime per line. There is no last_verified on this axis: nothing in this tree reads a newest-PHP scalar, and an invariant with no reader is decoration.

database.note: Each key of engines is a claimed database engine and its value the min-inclusive/max-exclusive version line that engine is claimed on; an engine this map does not name is refused (platform_database_engine_unsupported) rather than compared against another engine's range, and each version diagnostic names its engine because the range is now a function of the engine. There is deliberately no verified series map here, unlike the php and wordpress axes: each entry already names exactly one measured line, and the engines map already forces an engine-by-engine decision, so a third series map would prevent no failure. MariaDB 11.x is pinned by the sandbox harness's own Docker tag (mariadb:11 -- see sandbox/db.yml, sandbox/docker-compose.yml); verified live: 11.8.8-MariaDB as of this writing. MySQL is pinned to exactly the 8.4 LTS line the harness boots (mysql:8.4 -- sandbox/db.mysql.yml:60, selected with DUO_DB_ENGINE=mysql); the max stops at 8.5.0 rather than 9.0.0 on purpose, because a wider bound would admit innovation series nobody ran. PENDING as of this writing: the MySQL live proof (sandbox/tests/live/regress_core_scope_database.sh, plus regress_core_data_boundary.sh and conformance-core under DUO_DB_ENGINE=mysql) has NOT yet run -- what is green is the offline half plus a source-level MySQL 8.4 dialect audit of every SQL construct the agent sends (docs/mysql-dialect-audit.md), whose five probe groups are that suite's assertions verbatim. If the live matrix fails, the remedy is to drop the MySQL entry and restore a MariaDB-only engines map, never to widen around a failure.

wordpress.note: Pinned by the sandbox harness's exact Docker tags: each key of verified is a core series, and its value is the exact patch a full live proof ran on (6.9 on wordpress:6.9.2-php8.3-apache, 7.0 on wordpress:7.0.3-php8.3-apache, 7.1 on wordpress:7.1-php8.3-apache @sha256:65919a9ca10940feb10d9400fead0d639bf86241f47c91e2b9ea4703aa8452cf -- sandbox/tests/live/regress_core_scope_platform.sh, regress_core_data_boundary.sh, conformance-core). The 7.1 value is the literal two-component string WordPress itself ships for that series' first release (wp-includes/version.php:19 reads $wp_version = '7.1'); that is what get_bloginfo('version') returns and what this gate compares, so "7.1.0" would name a WordPress that does not exist. PENDING as of this writing: the 7.1 live proof (matrix, data boundary, conformance-core) has NOT yet run -- the offline half and a source-level 7.1 audit of every assumption manifests/core.json makes are green, and the exercise cell is wired. If the live matrix fails, the remedy is to drop the 7.1 entry and restore max 7.1.0 / last_verified 7.0.3, never to widen around a failure. A core is accepted only when it is inside [6.9.0, 7.2.0) AND its MAJOR.MINOR is one of those exercised series, so an unexercised minor line inside the range is still refused rather than claimed by a bare range. Patches inside an exercised series are claimed on exactly the basis PHP 8.3.x and MariaDB 11.x already are here -- one measured runtime per line. last_verified is the newest exercised core and the one sandbox/pair.yml boots by default.
